ossification.def: The formation of bone tissue by osteoblasts, also called osteogenesis. It begins at an ossification center and follows one of two routes: intramembranous or endochondral.

intramembranous-ossification.def: Bone formation directly within a sheet of mesenchyme, with no cartilage stage. It forms the flat bones of the skull roof, most bones of the face and the collarbones.

endochondral-ossification.def: Bone formation in which a hyaline cartilage model is broken down and replaced by bone, starting at a primary ossification center in the diaphysis and later at secondary ossification centers in the epiphyses. It forms most of the skeleton.

epiphyseal-plate.def: The disc of hyaline cartilage between the epiphysis and diaphysis of a growing long bone (the growth plate). Its four zones (reserve zone, proliferative zone, zone of maturation and hypertrophy, zone of calcified matrix) add cartilage that bone replaces; when growth ends it becomes the epiphyseal line.

bone-growth.def: Long bones lengthen by interstitial growth of cartilage at the epiphyseal plates, which bone then replaces, and widen by appositional growth: osteoblasts add bone under the periosteum while osteoclasts remove bone inside.
